ADJIA.why: Down about 13% from the ₹74 issue price on a business that has almost disappeared: revenue was about ₹0.24 crore in FY25 and near zero in FY26, with a quarterly net loss of about ₹0.25 crore and trailing EPS of -₹1.42. It sells augmented reality, virtual reality and 360° content. Trading is thin and the price is volatile (beta about 2.3).
ADJIA.outlook: No management guidance or analyst view was found. The market cap is only about ₹5-6 crore, so liquidity and survival of the business are the main risks.

NIKS.why: Up about 2x from the ₹201 issue price, but the business is small and shrinking: FY26 revenue fell to about ₹6.9 crore from ₹9.1 crore and profit to ₹0.20 crore from ₹0.45 crore. Price moves track corporate events: a proposed fundraise through equity and warrants (approved at the AGM) and a mandatory open offer for 26% at ₹136 a share from acquirers seeking control. It rebounded from a ₹276.5 low in July 2026.
NIKS.outlook: No guidance found. The preferential issue and open-offer filings are the best guide to direction. The open-offer price of ₹136 is far below the trading price, which is worth checking in the offer letter. It sells software, education services and drone trading.

NPST.why: A fintech and UPI infrastructure company that rose from ₹80 at issue (about ₹27 after split adjustment) to over ₹1,800. It gained about 69% in the six months to September 2026 even though FY26 profit fell: revenue was ₹208.6 crore (₹180.3 crore a year earlier) and net profit ₹41.1 crore (₹45.2 crore). No source tied the 2026 rally to a specific event; the company built a UPI stack for banks (2022) and a UPI credit card switch (2023), and has been reported to be moving to the mainboard.
NPST.outlook: No analyst targets or guidance found. The stock trades near 63x reported earnings (on FY26 EPS of ₹20.7 closer to 85-90x), far above large IT peers at about 19-22x, so it prices in growth the profits do not yet show. 52-week range ₹850-2,064.

NAAPBOOKS.why: More than doubled the ₹74 issue price. FY26 revenue rose 43.6% to about ₹18 crore and profit 85% to about ₹8 crore; it sells finance technology, mobile and web applications to corporates, is almost debt free and trades near 20x earnings. The shares rose 9.85% on 12 October 2026 with no specific catalyst identified, after a June 2026 low of ₹70. In June the board forfeited ₹2.26 crore of unpaid warrant money.
NAAPBOOKS.outlook: No guidance or analyst view found. Liquidity is thin (some days with no trades), and promoter holding fell in the latest quarter. Figures come from aggregator sites, not filings.

QUADPRO.why: Fell about 80% from the ₹20 issue price; a five-year return of about -76%. The best explanations found date from late 2025 and are generic (reduced investor participation, negative sentiment), not results or news. The market cap is only about ₹12 crore and the P/E of 60 rests on thin earnings.
QUADPRO.outlook: No 2026 results, broker research or guidance found. Promoters hold 65.9%. Check the company's filings; the data here is mostly from aggregator pages that disagree on the 52-week range.

CWD.why: Up about 54% on the ₹180 issue price. FY26 revenue jumped 343% to about ₹146 crore (a second report says ₹151 crore) and profit rose 391% to about ₹12 crore on rapid growth in soundbox deployments, smart infrastructure and IoT work. Margins were squeezed by higher material costs. The share is below its ₹425 52-week high.
CWD.outlook: Management sees a quarterly revenue run-rate of about ₹95-100 crore during FY27 if capacity ramps up, helped by an order for about 1 million CNIC communication units (about ₹45 crore), 40,000 weather stations for Jio and a walkie-talkie tie-up. It depends on execution; reports differ on exact revenue so check filings.

WHERRELZ.why: Down about 21% from the ₹171 issue price and at its 52-week low of ₹135 (high ₹252.50); down 32% over a year. Trailing net profit is about -₹9 crore, book value is negative and ROCE is -21%. Promoters own only about 20.5%. It sells web IT products and consulting, ERP, cybersecurity, IoT and cloud tools.
WHERRELZ.outlook: No guidance, forecast or analyst view found. The loss-making financial condition is the main concern in the data. Market cap is about ₹5 crore.

VIVO.why: Nearly doubled the ₹82 issue price, with most of the move in 2026 (about ₹73-77 in February-July, then ₹150-164 by August-September; +138% over a year). No source explained the rally. The business has shrunk: the voice platform was closed from 31 March 2025 as unviable and it now says it is building technology suites for EV chargers. It is loss-making and promoters hold 73.4%.
VIVO.outlook: No guidance, analyst forecasts or recent results found. A small free float can make a thinly traded stock swing on modest buying (my inference). Market cap is only about ₹30 crore on a loss-making base.

EKENNIS.why: Down about 49% from the ₹72 issue price after a spike in 2026 (₹142-150 in April, ₹116 in June, ₹69.65 in August, ₹36.75 now). ROE is -38% and five-year sales growth is -14.9%. The sources gave no results or news for the 2026 moves. It sells software consulting and products, training, and digital and 3D printing and packaging.
EKENNIS.outlook: No guidance, forecasts or analyst view found. The 52-week range of ₹37-168 shows how volatile it is. The results of the 25 May 2026 board meeting were not in the sources.
